correctness.rationale: For a word with z zeros, o ones, and zero/one run counts r0,r1, the length-two composition counts are a=z-r0, b=o-r1, and mixed count t=r0+r1-1 for nonconstant words, so the observation is equivalent to (z,r0,r1). Feasible pairs satisfy |r0-r1|<=1; counting symbol totals over balanced and one-heavy run-count pairs yields the two closed forms. Positive compositions of z and o into run lengths give the stated class sizes and singleton criterion. An independent brute-force reconstruction for every binary word through n=12 reproduced the observation partition, closed forms, class sizes, and singleton sets exactly; the package verifier extends corroborative brute force to n=16 and arithmetic checks to n=500.

value.rationale: This resolves the first nontrivial constant-r case explicitly singled out by the defining paper as an open direction, and it does so completely: not only the asymptotic capacity but the exact all-n number of observations, every ambiguity-class size, and all individually reconstructible words. That is a natural structural base case likely to be useful in any study of fixed r.
residual_risks: The methods are special to r=2 and may not extend cleanly to r>=3.

final_claim: For binary reconstruction from the multiset of compositions of all contiguous substrings of lengths one and two, the number of distinct observations is \(R_2(2m)=3m^2-2m+2\) and \(R_2(2m+1)=3m^2+m+2\), with the stated exact ambiguity-class size formulas and complete singleton-class classification.
limitations: The alphabet is binary and the observation length cutoff is exactly \(r=2\).
No exact formula for \(r\ge3\), nonbinary alphabets, or noisy composition multisets is claimed.
